description: WolverineFx (multi-transport: PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, or Azure Service Bus) provider for the Brainograph.Messaging seam. References only Brainograph.Messaging.Abstractions + WolverineFx (+ WolverineFx.Postgresql/WolverineFx.RabbitMQ/WolverineFx.AzureServiceBus for the transport-specific strategies).
releaseNotes: 2.2.1 — a Wolverine host that is still starting now has an owner (bg-shared#21). WolverineHostFactory.DisposeAsync did nothing until StartAsync had published its host, so a dispose that landed mid-start (a consumer stopped while its host was still provisioning) left the host that start went on to finish running with no owner, and a start that threw or was cancelled never stopped or disposed the host it had built. Against Postgres every such host keeps its own connection pool; the defect was found while diagnosing bg-media#28, whose integration suite exhausted Postgres connections (SQLSTATE 53300). Now DisposeAsync cancels and awaits an in-flight start; a host that was built but not published is stopped and disposed before StartAsync returns (a teardown failure there is logged as a warning, never thrown over the start's own exception); and WolverineMessageConsumer.Consume disposes the host it started when it returns or throws, instead of leaving it to the consumer's Dispose. StartAsync on a factory whose DisposeAsync has begun throws ObjectDisposedException instead of building a host nobody would dispose. Timing: in a hosted service that cancels Consume before closing the consumer, the Wolverine host now stops and drains inside Consume's finally, which the host's shutdown token bounds, and a later Close or Dispose finds nothing to do; before, Close stopped the host synchronously with no bound. No public API change. Not in this release: PostgresTransportStrategy.ProvisionAsync still ignores its cancellation token, so a cancelled Postgres start waits out the schema migration before its host is discarded. 2.2.0 — the Wolverine host no longer builds a logging stack of its own. Host.CreateDefaultBuilder() installed console plus, on Windows, the EventLog provider, giving every service a SECOND logging pipeline that the application never configured: it read Logging:LogLevel independently of the outer Serilog host (so the two disagreed about what was worth logging, and the log budget was set by the one nobody tuned), it bypassed Serilog entirely (so those lines carried no service name and no trace id), and Wolverine's EndpointCollection.DrainAsync logged at shutdown into an already-disposed EventLog provider — an ObjectDisposedException that presented as a flaky Windows test rather than a bug. The inner builder now clears its providers, and where the application has an ILoggerFactory it is lent to the host so Wolverine logs through the same pipeline as everything else. The factory is wrapped so the inner container cannot dispose it: a container disposes the singletons it holds, and disposing the application's factory would silence the WHOLE application after a messaging restart. API: WolverineHostFactory takes an optional trailing ILoggerFactory (existing positional callers are unaffected), and WolverineMessageConsumer takes one via DI. Omitting it means the host logs nowhere — deliberately preferred over reinstating console/EventLog. 2.1.1 — fixes a benign teardown race in the soft-boot producer hosted service (introduced with the soft-boot change in 2.0.1): under WebApplicationFactory disposal the host could Dispose() the hosted service — disposing its stopping CancellationTokenSource — before/without an orderly StopAsync, so StopAsync's `_stopping.CancelAsync()` threw ObjectDisposedException. StopAsync now guards only that CTS interaction so the stop path is idempotent and dispose-safe in any interleaving; real process shutdown was never affected, but downstream test factories no longer need a scoped catch. No API change. 2.1.0 — adds an OPT-IN durable outbox for the brokered transports (RabbitMq/ASB), the fix for the 2.0.x sender-side at-least-once gap: set `Messaging:Wolverine:DurableOutbox:Enabled=true` (+ `:ConnectionString`, typically the service's own app DB, and optional `:Schema`, default `messaging`). It adds a Postgres message store, and the producer's durable send path enlists a fresh MessageContext in a store transaction and publishes via BroadcastToTopicAsync (a ROUTED send — a bare EndpointFor(uri).SendAsync bypasses the outbox), so the outgoing envelope is PERSISTED to wolverine_outgoing_envelopes on commit and forwarded by the durability agent — a broker OUTAGE no longer loses the produce (proven by DurableOutboxBrokerOutageTests: produce during a stop_app outage lands in the store and is delivered exactly-once after start_app). Off by default → 2.0.x behaviour (broker-native durability, documented gap) is unchanged for anyone who does not set it. 2.0.0 — transport config-selectable via `Messaging:Wolverine:Transport`; RabbitMQ + ASB transports (native fan-out); same consume-side contract on all three. See MESSAGING-TRANSPORTS.md §4.4.
